name: Level_1 - Task_10
description: Evaluate the in-plane mechanical stiffness of graphene using the MACE-MP-0 interatomic potential. Construct a primitive graphene unit cell containing two carbon atoms using ASE's graphene builder with lattice parameter a = 2.46 Å and 15 Å of vacuum along the z-axis. Attach the MACE-MP-0 calculator and perform a constrained geometric relaxation of the atomic positions and unit cell. Allow the in-plane cell components to relax while keeping the out-of-plane cell dimension and cell components fixed, using ASE's ExpCellFilter with the mask [True, True, False, False, False, True]. Optimize with BFGS until the maximum force is below 0.005 eV/Å. After relaxation, calculate the equilibrium in-plane cell area as A_0 = |a_1 × a_2|. Generate 11 biaxially strained configurations by scaling both relaxed in-plane lattice vectors by factors from 0.98 to 1.02 in uniform increments of 0.004. Scale the atomic coordinates proportionally in the xy-plane while keeping the 15 Å z-direction vacuum unchanged. Do not perform further relaxation of the strained configurations. For each strained configuration, calculate the total potential energy with MACE. Fit the resulting energy-area data to E(A) = aA² + bA + c. Calculate the 2D in-plane stiffness as K_2D = 2aA_0. Convert the resulting value from eV/Å² to N/m using 1 eV/Å² = 16.0217662 N/m, and return K_2D as a single floating-point value in N/m. Use ASE, MACE, and the BFGS optimizer.
